provinces.name: British Columbia
provinces.where: Applied Design, Skills & Technologies (ADST) — required K–9, electives 10–12; Career Education; Digital Literacy Framework
provinces.notes: Ministry guidance 'Digital literacy and the use of AI in education' encourages critical, ethical use. Vancouver School Board approved Microsoft Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection for staff and secondary students.

provinces.name: New Brunswick
provinces.where: AI literacy woven across K–12 curriculum from September 2026 (first province to do so)
provinces.notes: Focus on critical thinking, ethics and responsible use rather than a stand-alone course.

provinces.name: Ontario
provinces.where: Board-level AI guidelines; digital literacy in Language (2023) and Math curricula
provinces.notes: No province-wide AI course; boards such as TDSB and Peel publish staff/student AI guidance.

provinces.name: Alberta
provinces.where: Career & Technology Foundations; host of Amii and the National AI Literacy Initiative launch (Edmonton)
provinces.notes: Educators can access 'Essentials for Educators' free from Amii.

provinces.name: Manitoba
provinces.where: School-level modules, e.g. Winnipeg collegiate 2-hour AI literacy module
provinces.notes: Provincial guidance under development; strong school-led practice.

provinces.name: Quebec
provinces.where: Digital Competency Framework (Cadre de référence de la compétence numérique)
provinces.notes: Ministry guidance on generative AI in schools (French-first).

provinces.name: Federal (pan-Canadian)
provinces.where: National AI Literacy Initiative ($13M, Amii, Sept 2026) · CanCode Phase 5 ($30M, 2026–2028) · AI for All strategy
provinces.notes: Education is provincial; federal programs fund resources and training rather than mandating curriculum.
